note: Condition groups recognised on any plant by the plant-identification model. Treatments are general; check the label and the plant's sensitivity first.

conditions.symptoms: No disease or pest symptoms detected. Leaf colour and texture look normal for this plant.
organic: No treatment needed
prevention: Check the underside of leaves once a week for insects
Water at the base, in the morning
Give the plant the light it needs and avoid waterlogged pots
Remove dead or fallen leaves

conditions.pathogen: e.g. Cercospora, Alternaria, Colletotrichum (anthracnose), Diplocarpon (rose black spot), Xanthomonas
conditions.symptoms: Brown, black or tan spots, often with a yellow halo, that grow and merge into dead (blighted) patches; leaves may yellow and drop early. Spreads in warm, wet weather.
chemical: Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5 g/L) or copper oxychloride 50 WP (3 g/L), 2–3 sprays 10 days apart
For anthracnose / black spot: carbendazim 50 WP (1 g/L) or hexaconazole 5 EC (1 mL/L)
organic: Remove and destroy spotted leaves; do not compost them
Spray neem oil 5 mL/L with a few drops of liquid soap
Baking-soda spray (5 g/L) as a preventive
Trichoderma-enriched compost at the root zone
prevention: Avoid wetting leaves; water at the base
Space and prune plants for air flow
Clear fallen leaves before and after the monsoon
Disinfect pruning tools

conditions.symptoms: White to grey powdery patches on leaves, young shoots and buds; leaves curl, yellow and dry. Common in dry days with cool, humid nights (winter in central India).
chemical: Wettable sulphur 80 WP (2–3 g/L) – avoid above 32 °C
Hexaconazole 5 EC (1 mL/L) or propiconazole 25 EC (1 mL/L)
organic: Milk spray (1 part milk : 9 parts water) on sunny mornings
Baking soda 5 g/L + a few drops of soap
Neem oil 5 mL/L every 7 days
Prune heavily infected shoots
prevention: Plant in full sun with good spacing
Avoid excess nitrogen fertiliser
Remove infected leaves early

conditions.symptoms: Small orange, yellow or brown powdery pustules, mostly on the underside of leaves, with pale spots above; heavy infection dries the leaves.
chemical: Propiconazole 25 EC (1 mL/L) or tebuconazole 25.9 EC (1 mL/L) as curative
organic: Pick and destroy leaves with pustules
Sulphur dust or wettable sulphur (2 g/L)
Neem oil 5 mL/L
prevention: Water early so leaves dry quickly
Remove alternate weed hosts
Grow resistant varieties for crops such as wheat

conditions.pathogen: Capnodiaceae and related fungi growing on insect honeydew
conditions.symptoms: Black, soot-like coating on the upper leaf surface that can be rubbed off. It grows on sticky honeydew from aphids, mealybugs, whiteflies or scale insects, which are the real cause.
chemical: Control the sucking insect: imidacloprid 17.8 SL (0.3 mL/L) or thiamethoxam 25 WG (0.3 g/L)
Starch spray (20 g/L) dries and flakes off the mould
organic: Wash leaves with mild soapy water
Neem oil 5 mL/L with soap to kill the insects producing honeydew
Control ants that protect the insects
prevention: Check for aphids, mealybugs and scale regularly
Prune crowded branches for light and air

conditions.pathogen: e.g. begomoviruses (leaf curl, yellow vein mosaic), potyviruses; similar mottling from iron, zinc or magnesium deficiency
conditions.symptoms: Yellow–green mosaic or mottled pattern, yellow veins, curled, puckered or small leaves and stunted growth. Viruses are spread by whiteflies, aphids or thrips and cannot be cured.
chemical: No cure for viruses – control the insect vector: imidacloprid 17.8 SL (0.3 mL/L) or spiromesifen (whiteflies)
If deficiency is suspected: chelated micronutrient spray (Fe/Zn) as per label
organic: Remove and destroy clearly infected plants early
Yellow sticky traps for whiteflies and aphids
Neem oil 5 mL/L against vectors
Add compost / micronutrients and check soil pH
prevention: Use virus-free seedlings and resistant varieties
Control weeds that host vectors
Keep new plants separate for a week before placing them with others

conditions.pathogen: e.g. mealybugs, aphids, whiteflies, scale insects, spider mites, citrus leaf miner
conditions.symptoms: White cottony clusters (mealybugs), small green/black insects on shoots (aphids), tiny white flies under leaves, brown bumps on stems (scale), fine webbing and speckling (mites) or silvery tunnels in leaves (leaf miner). Leaves curl, yellow and get sticky.
chemical: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (0.3 mL/L) for aphids, whiteflies, mealybugs
Dicofol / abamectin as per label for mites
Spinosad (as per label) for leaf miners
organic: Spray a strong jet of water to dislodge insects
Neem oil 5 mL/L + soap, every 5–7 days
Wipe mealybugs and scale with cotton dipped in alcohol
Yellow sticky traps; encourage ladybird beetles
prevention: Inspect new plants before bringing them home
Avoid excess nitrogen that produces soft shoots
Keep ants away from the plant
